# OsStringView

A borrowed run of native units.

```rux
pub struct OsStringView {
    pub units: OsUnit[..];
}
```

`Copy`, owning nothing. The units it names must outlive it.

<h3 id="equals"><code>Equals</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Equals(
    self: &OsStringView,
    other: &OsStringView
) -> bool
```

Whether two views hold the same units.
Unit equality and nothing smarter: no case folding, no normalization. Two names the filesystem treats as
one are still two names here, because which names those are is the filesystem's opinion, not the string's.

| Name    | Type            | Description                  |
| ------- | --------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `other` | `&OsStringView` | the value to compare against |

**Returns**: whether both hold the same units in the same order

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Path/Src/OsString.rux#L77)

<h3 id="to-text"><code>ToText</code></h3>

```rux
pub func ToText(
    self: &OsStringView,
    allocator: Allocator
) -> String ! TextError
```

This native text as UTF-8, or nothing where it is not text.
The fallible direction, and fallible for a different reason per platform: Unix bytes may simply not be
UTF-8, and Windows units may hold an unpaired surrogate, which no UTF-8 sequence can spell. It fails with
`InvalidUtf8` for both, because both mean the same thing to the caller — this name is not text, and a
program that must show it anyway shows it lossily by its own policy, knowingly.

| Name        | Type        | Description                  |
| ----------- | ----------- | ---------------------------- |
| `allocator` | `Allocator` | where the storage comes from |

**Returns**: the units converted to text, or a failure when they are not valid in it

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Path/Src/OsString.rux#L95)

## Implements Display

`OsStringView` conforms to `Display`.

<h3 id="write-display"><code>WriteDisplay</code></h3>

```rux
pub func WriteDisplay(
    self: &OsStringView,
    writer: &var TextWriter,
    spec: FormatSpec
) -> ! FormatError
```

Writes the name as text, with every native unit that is not text replaced by U+FFFD.
Lossy, deliberately and only here. A name the system holds is not obliged to be text, and a program
reporting which file it could not open still has to name it; U+FFFD is what the standard provides for
exactly that. What this produces is for a reader, never for reopening the file — two different names can
render alike, and `Debug` is the rendering that does not.
Reports whatever the writer reported, and `UnsupportedRequest` for any style or precision. A precision is
refused rather than applied because a truncated path is a different path, and may be one that exists.

| Name     | Type              | Description                    |
| -------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `writer` | `&var TextWriter` | the destination                |
| `spec`   | `FormatSpec`      | what the placeholder asked for |

**Returns**: success when the whole name was accepted

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Path/Src/OsString.rux#L208)

## Implements Debug

`OsStringView` conforms to `Debug`.

<h3 id="write-debug"><code>WriteDebug</code></h3>

```rux
pub func WriteDebug(
    self: &OsStringView,
    writer: &var TextWriter,
    spec: FormatSpec
) -> ! FormatError
```

Writes the name exactly, quoted, with every unit that is not text spelled as an escape.
Nothing is lost: a Unix byte outside a well-formed sequence is written `\x{nn}` and a Windows code unit
with no partner is written `\u{xxxx}`, so the native units can be read back off the output and two
different names never render alike. The quote, the backslash and the control characters are escaped the way
this repository escapes them everywhere else.
Reports whatever the writer reported, and `UnsupportedRequest` for any style or precision.

| Name     | Type              | Description                    |
| -------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `writer` | `&var TextWriter` | the destination                |
| `spec`   | `FormatSpec`      | what the placeholder asked for |

**Returns**: success when the whole name was accepted

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Path/Src/OsString.rux#L226)
